title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Groupes de Galois motiviques commutatifs'. Setting: k a field; M the Tannakian category of (iso)motives over k with Q-coefficients, assumed semisimple. G is the band (lien) of M and 𝒢 the gerbe of fibre functors on M, so M ≃ Rep(𝒢). The word 'supposé commutatif' after the band is crossed out, so here the band is general; the title suggests the commutative (abelian/CM-type) case is the eventual goal.

(1) Tate part. M_0 ⊂ M is the Tannakian subcategory generated by the Tate motive Q(1). Its gerbe 𝒢_0 has band G_0 = G_m. The inclusion M_0 ⊂ M gives an epimorphism of gerbes 𝒢 → 𝒢_0 and of bands ε: G → G_m (the Tate/cyclotomic character). 𝒢_0 is neutral: a Q-valued fibre functor φ on M_0 is fixed by choosing a generator of the fibre of Q(1) (the struck-through 'Q(1) → Q'). By Hilbert 90, H^1(Q, G_m) = 0, so any two Q-valued fibre functors on M_0 are isomorphic.

(2) Band reduction. Fix such a trivialisation φ of 𝒢_0. Consider fibre functors ω on M together with an isomorphism ω|_{M_0} ≅ φ. These form a new gerbe 𝒢_φ = 𝒢 ×_{𝒢_0} (pt), whose band is U = Ker(ε). This is the standard reduction of a gerbe to the kernel of a morphism of bands when the image gerbe is neutralised; the margin note says 'vérif Giraud!'.

(3) Finite (Artin) part. M' ⊂ M is the full subcategory of objects X such that the tensor constructions on X ⊕ X̌ involve only finitely many simple objects (up to isomorphism). These are the objects of 'finite type', whose Tannakian group is finite. 𝒢' and G' are the corresponding gerbe and band, with an epimorphism 𝒢 → 𝒢' and an exact sequence 1 → G° → G → G' → 1. The kernel G° is the neutral component. M' is identified with (a full subcategory of) Artin motives over k, so G' corresponds to the profinite Galois group Gal(k̄/k). The page breaks off as he starts to describe the points of k̄ as a (finite) set or Galois-set, presumably to make the Artin-motive side explicit.

Purpose: to set up the structure of the motivic Galois gerbe through two dévissages. One is the weight/Tate character G → G_m with kernel U. The other is the extension of the Galois group (π_0) by the connected component G°. These prepare a study of the commutative case, i.e. what later became the Serre group and Taniyama group picture for CM/abelian motives.
errors: Semisimplicity of the category of motives was then conjectural (it follows from standard conjectures; Jannsen 1992 later proved it for numerical equivalence). It is assumed here, not proved.

Fibre functors over general Q-schemes S on M_0 are only locally isomorphic, since Pic(S) need not vanish. The Hilbert 90 remark only gives uniqueness up to isomorphism of Q-valued (field-valued) fibre functors. That suffices for neutrality of 𝒢_0, which is the point used.
'Equivalent to a full subcategory of Artin motives': with the definition given, M' should be equivalent to the whole category of Artin motives (with Q-coefficients). The hedge is harmless.
The trivialisation of 𝒢_0 is canonical only up to the choice of a fibre of Q(1), i.e. up to G_m(Q) = Q^×. Hence 𝒢_φ depends on φ up to a non-canonical isomorphism.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois gerbe of fibre functors with band G; Tannakian formalism for motives over a non-algebraically-closed coefficient situation
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois gerbe / Tannakian gerbe (non-neutral Tannakian category)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra's thesis; Récoltes et Semailles describes them retrospectively

ideas.what: Tate subcategory M_0 generated by Q(1), with gerbe banded by G_m and epimorphism ε: G → G_m (Tate/weight character); neutrality via Hilbert 90
ideas.modern_name: Tate (cyclotomic) character of the motivic Galois group; the weight cocharacter is its dual counterpart

ideas.what: Reduction of the band of a gerbe from G to U = Ker ε by fixing a fibre functor on M_0 (fibre product 𝒢 ×_{𝒢_0} pt)
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of structure of a gerbe along an exact sequence of bands (Giraud, Cohomologie non abélienne)

ideas.what: Artin motives as the finite-type part; exact sequence 1 → G° → G → Gal(k̄/k) → 1
ideas.modern_name: π_0 of the motivic Galois group = absolute Galois group (Artin motives); connected component G°

ideas.what: Programme of studying commutative motivic Galois groups (title)
ideas.modern_name: Serre group (Galois group of CM/abelian motives) and Taniyama group (extension of Gal by Serre group)

missed.claim: This page shows Grothendieck himself setting up the two dévissages of the motivic Galois gerbe. One is the Tate character with kernel U, obtained by band reduction after neutralising the Tate gerbe. The other is the π_0 sequence via Artin motives, as a preparation for 'commutative motivic Galois groups'. This is the skeleton later used for the Serre group and Taniyama group, here in gerbe language with explicit band reduction. If the page dates from 1965, it predates Serre 1968 and Saavedra 1972. Mathematically everything here is now standard.
missed.quote: Une trivialisation de 𝒢_0 permet de restreindre les liens de 𝒢 de G à Ker ε = U
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution: it documents that the gerbe-theoretic formulation of the weight/Tate and Artin dévissages of the motivic Galois group is Grothendieck's. The mathematics itself is not new.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard Tannakian structure of the motivic Galois group: Tate character, band reduction, and Artin motives giving π_0. All of this is in Saavedra and Deligne–Milne. The interest is purely historical (early, gerbe-theoretic, oriented toward the commutative/CM case), and the page stops before anything specifically commutative appears.
transcription_corrections: 'Leur forme une nouvelle gerbe' should probably read 'Ils forment une nouvelle gerbe'.

In the definition of M', 'combinaisons de puissances d'objets simples' is more plausibly 'combinaisons d'un nombre fini d'objets simples'. The underlined interlinear line contains '𝒢' la gerbe associée, G' le lien' rather than 'sommes de droites'.

'𝒢_0 est trivialisée canoniquement d'une manière' is uncertain. The sense is that 𝒢_0 is trivialised, unique up to isomorphism, by the choice of a fibre functor φ on M_0, possibly '(non canoniquement)'.
'sont {+?+} isomorphes': the interlinear word above 'sont' is likely 'canoniquement' or 'toujours'; the meaning is that the fibre functors are isomorphic.
Neighbouring page reference: 'G_1' on p.133 probably corresponds to the same set-up (G, 𝒢), drafted earlier.
